findings.reason: Verified that OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key copies Paginator's math.floor/ceil logic (paginator.py:838-840) and the endpoint orders by a datetime, so math.floor on a datetime raises TypeError whenever optimized_pagination=true returns rows; DateTimePaginator (paginator.py:233-236) is the correct base.

Verified RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is Optional (model.py:346) and line 71 dereferences it unconditionally, outside the use_optimized check, so a non-superuser with no membership row gets an AttributeError on every request.

Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative start indices with ValueError, so the enable_advanced_features branch turns a client-supplied negative cursor offset into an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 BadPaginationError.

Checking request.user.is_superuser versus is_active_superuser is a legitimate authorization-consistency concern, but it is advisory and the endpoint is already gated by OrganizationAuditPermission, so no concrete escalation is shown.

The comment in BasePaginator is indeed false for prev cursors with negative offsets, but that crash already existed before this PR because the prev branch was unchanged, so the PR only makes it a documentation-level mismatch.
The Cursor comment is misleading about negative offsets being an intended feature, but it is only a comment and cannot break behaviour.
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result, which is a maintainability concern rather than a defect.
The PR adds no tests, and the missing tests would have caught the verified TypeError in get_item_key and the member dereference, but this is still a test gap rather than a defect in the code itself.
